pamphlet_excerpts: Different American Indian cultural areas: From the brief descriptions in this pamphlet, you have learnedsome of the difficulties American Indian tribes faced after thearrival of Europeans (p. 91).
Different American Indian cultural areas Principle 2: Native peoples lost so much that by thelate 19th and early 20th centuries, it seemed to some observers that they must be doomed (p. 91).
Different American Indian cultural areas Principle 3: Others lost huge numbers of their people and all of their lands and possessions (p. 91).

Different American Indian cultural areas Principle 4: Some, like the Mission Indians of California, lost cultural memories, their Indian ways of living and s­ urviving, after being undermissionary (p. 91).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Different American Indian cultural areas): Some people predicted that eventually all Indian cultures and their traditional ways would be lost and that finally the Indians themselves (p. 91).
Step 2 (Different American Indian cultural areas): Native peoples endured, and today there are about 2 million American Indians living in the United States (p. 91).
Step 3 (Different American Indian cultural areas): Today, more than half of American Indians live outside the reservations that were set aside for them by the federalgovernment (p. 91).
Step 4 (Different American Indian cultural areas): Many live in big cities; others live in smallercommunities and rural areas (p. 91).

pamphlet_excerpts: American Indian Tribe: An American Indian tribe, group: Indians are relearning lost traditions and languages and revivingtheir arts and crafts, their songs, dances, and stories (p. 71).

American Indian Tribe Principle 2: An American Indian tribe, group Principle 2: Many havechosen not to disappear into America's "melting pot." Indians are reclaiming control over what happens to them (p. 71).
American Indian Tribe Principle 3: An American Indian tribe, group Principle 3: They want to decide for themselves how they will live in themodern world (p. 71).

American Indian Tribe Principle 4: An American Indian tribe, group Principle 4: The question is, how can they keep cultural roots alive and protect and preserve tribal identities, yet still be a part ofmodern society (p. 71).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (American Indian Tribe): Step 1 (An American Indian tribe, group): There is no easy answer, and no one knowswhat the future holds (p. 71).

Step 2 (American Indian Tribe): Step 2 (An American Indian tribe, group): The history of American Indians is filled with the names ofmen and women who are remembered for deeds that set themapart from others (p. 71).
Step 3 (American Indian Tribe): Step 3 (An American Indian tribe, group): They may have been renowned leaders, peacemakers, or lawmakers (p. 71).
Step 4 (American Indian Tribe): Step 4 (An American Indian tribe, group): Some, like Pocahontas, Sacajawea, Hahyonhwatha (known as "Hiawatha"), and Tecumseh, livedcenturies ago (p. 71).

pamphlet_excerpts: Museum Either In-person or Virtually: Visit a museum either in-person: Indians are relearning lost traditions and languages and revivingtheir arts and crafts, their songs, dances, and stories (p. 37).

Museum Either In-person or Virtually Principle 2: Visit a museum either in-person Principle 2: Many havechosen not to disappear into America's "melting pot." Indians are reclaiming control over what happens to them (p. 37).
Museum Either In-person or Virtually Principle 3: Visit a museum either in-person Principle 3: They want to decide for themselves how they will live in themodern world (p. 37).

Museum Either In-person or Virtually Principle 4: Visit a museum either in-person Principle 4: The question is, how can they keep cultural roots alive and protect and preserve tribal identities, yet still be a part ofmodern society (p. 37).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Museum Either In-person or Virtually): Step 1 (Visit a museum either in-person): There is no easy answer, and no one knowswhat the future holds (p. 37).

Step 2 (Museum Either In-person or Virtually): Step 2 (Visit a museum either in-person): The history of American Indians is filled with the names ofmen and women who are remembered for deeds that set themapart from others (p. 37).
Step 3 (Museum Either In-person or Virtually): Step 3 (Visit a museum either in-person): They may have been renowned leaders, peacemakers, or lawmakers (p. 37).

Step 4 (Museum Either In-person or Virtually): Step 4 (Visit a museum either in-person): Some, like Pocahontas, Sacajawea, Hahyonhwatha (known as "Hiawatha"), and Tecumseh, livedcenturies ago (p. 37).
